mainTopic: What תחת means when exchanging holy and non-holy animals, the chain of questions about mixed groups of animals, and whether paying the difference when redeeming a blemished animal is a תורה law.
overview: The גמרא shows that the word תחת ('in place of') can mean two things. It can mean the holiness stays and spreads to the new animal, as in תמורה, or it can mean the holiness moves off one item onto another (אחולי). Context decides: with קדשי מזבח it means תמורה, and with קדשי בדק הבית it means moving the holiness. רבא and רב אשי add that a blemished holy animal can go either way, depending on which animal the owner's hand rests on. אביי, and later רב אשי, then ask a chain of questions about groups of holy and non-holy animals, where a person says 'these are in place of those.' Each question tests the rule that a person does not leave a permitted act to do a forbidden one. The chain ends with תיקו, unresolved. Next the גמרא quotes the משנה about redeeming a blemished holy animal. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether paying הקדש the difference in value is a תורה law or a rabbinic one. The גמרא then tries to pin down what price gap they are arguing about.

steps.title: A verse where תחת means staying in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about the בהרת to show that תחת can mean 'staying in its place.' This fits the idea of תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But if the white spot stays in its place (תַּחְתֶּיהָ).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show one meaning of the word תחת: something that stays where it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בהרת verse, תחתיה means the spot remains in its place. That matches תמורה, where the original holy animal keeps its holiness even though the new animal also becomes holy. So here תחת is a word of 'joining' holiness, not of moving it away.

keyTerms.meaning: In its place (from the word תַּחַת)
A white spot of צרעת on the skin
Exchanging a holy animal for a non-holy one; both end up holy

phrases.english: 'But if the white spot stays in its place.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:23. The point is that the spot stays put, just like the first animal keeps its holiness in תמורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תַּחְתֶּיהָ תַּעֲמוֹד הַבַּהֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about the meaning of the word תחת by giving a verse for the 'staying in place' meaning.
steps.raayaObject: That תחת can mean 'remaining in place,' as in תמורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 13:23, the בהרת that stays in its place

steps.title: A verse where תחת means replacing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that תחת also means replacing one thing with another, from the פסוק about gold replacing brass.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also a word of transferring holiness out, as it is written: 'In place of brass I will bring gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק that uses תחת in the opposite way, meaning 'swap out.' This sets up the problem the next step will solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיה, the brass is gone and gold comes in its place. That fits אחולי, where the holiness leaves one item and goes onto another. So now the word תחת seems to point both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Making something non-holy by moving its holiness onto something else
Brass/copper
Gold

phrases.english: [It is also a word] of transferring holiness out,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out some words here. It means the word תחת can also be a word of אחולי.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'In place of brass I will bring gold,'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַחוֹלֵי, דִּכְתִיב: תַּחַת הַנְּחוֹשֶׁת אָבִיא זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a verse showing the opposite meaning of תחת, which creates a tension with step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That תחת can mean replacement, as in אחולי
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה 60:17, 'in place of brass I will bring gold'

steps.title: The meaning depends on the type of holy item
steps.stepSummary: Since תחת can mean either thing, the גמרא decides by context. With קדשי מזבח, which can make a תמורה, it means joining holiness. With קדשי בדק הבית, which cannot make a תמורה, it means transferring holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, regarding altar offerings, which can make a substitute, it is a word of joining holiness. Regarding items given for Temple upkeep, which cannot make a substitute, it is a word of transferring holiness out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the two meanings by saying the right one depends on what kind of holy thing is being talked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי מזבח can make a תמורה, so saying תחת about them is read as spreading their holiness to the new animal. קדשי בדק הבית can never make a תמורה, so the only thing תחת could do there is move the holiness out (פדיון).

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
Animals set aside to be offered on the מזבח
Items given for the upkeep of the בית המקדש
Making holiness 'catch' onto something new, while the original stays holy

steps.whatToRemember: תחת is read by context: with קדשי מזבח it means תמורה (joining holiness), and with קדשי בדק הבית it means אחולי (transferring holiness).

phrases.english: And therefore, regarding altar offerings,
which can make a substitute,
it is a word of joining holiness;
regarding items given for Temple upkeep,
which cannot make a substitute,
it is a word of transferring holiness out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכָּךְ, גַּבֵּי קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ דְּעָבְדִין תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension between the two verses by assigning each meaning to a different kind of holy item.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by context (type of holy item)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word תחת seems to have two conflicting meanings.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each meaning applies in its own setting: תמורה for קדשי מזבח, and אחולי for קדשי בדק הבית.

steps.title: רבא: even altar offerings can mean transfer
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even with קדשי מזבח, תחת can mean transferring holiness. This happens when the holy animal is a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even with altar offerings, you can find it is a word of transferring holiness out, for example when the holy animal had a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds an exception to the rule from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A holy animal with a מום can no longer be offered, so it is allowed to be redeemed. So when its owner says תחת, he could mean redeeming it, even though it is קדשי מזבח. The general category stays the same; only the outcome in this case is different.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a blemish that makes it unfit for the מזבח
Something holy, set aside for the בית המקדש
You can find it (a case where it happens)

phrases.english: Rava said: Even with altar offerings
you can find that it is a word of transferring holiness out,
for example, where the holy animal had a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲפִילּוּ בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of step 3 by giving an exception within קדשי מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a blemished holy animal, even though it is קדשי מזבח, תחת can mean transferring holiness out.

steps.title: רב אשי: it depends on where his hand is
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even with a בעל מום, תחת can go either way. If the owner's hand is on the holy animal, he is transferring its holiness out. If his hand is on the non-holy animal, he is making it holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even with a blemished animal, you can find it as a word of transferring holiness and you can find it as a word of joining holiness. If his hand is on the holy animal, it becomes non-holy; if his hand is on the non-holy animal, it becomes holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי refines רבא's point further by giving a practical sign of what the owner means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a blemished animal both meanings are possible, so we look at where the owner's hand is resting. A hand on the holy animal shows he wants to free it from its holiness (חול). A hand on the non-holy animal shows he wants to make that one holy as a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: His hand
Non-holy, ordinary
Holy
Also

steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: context decides the meaning of תחת. With a בעל מום, the owner's hand shows what he means. A hand on the holy animal means it becomes חול, and a hand on the non-holy animal means it becomes קודש.
steps.confusionAlert: 'חול הוי' means the holy animal he is touching becomes non-holy, not the other animal. 'קודש הוי' means the non-holy animal he is touching becomes holy.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָשֵׁי: אֲפִילּוּ בְּבַעַל מוּם נָמֵי
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Even with a blemished animal too
you can find it as a word of transferring holiness out,
and you can find it as a word of joining holiness.
If his hand is on the holy animal, it becomes non-holy;
if his hand is on the non-holy animal, it becomes holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָשֵׁי: אֲפִילּוּ בְּבַעַל מוּם נָמֵי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines רבא's exception by showing that, even for a בעל מום, the meaning depends on where the owner's hand is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a blemished holy animal, the owner's hand decides the meaning. A hand on the holy animal means transfer (it becomes חול), and a hand on the non-holy animal means תמורה (it becomes קודש).

steps.title: אביי asks about blemished holy animals and unblemished non-holy animals
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: if there are two blemished holy animals and two unblemished non-holy animals, and a person says 'these are in place of those,' what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: There were two holy animals in front of him, both with a blemish, and two non-holy animals with no blemish. He said, 'These are in place of those.' What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי presents a new case and asks what the law is. This sets up the question, and the next step explains why it is unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said we can tell what תחת means by where the person's hand is. Here the person says 'these in place of those' over the whole group without touching any animal, so we cannot tell. The holy animals are blemished, so transferring their holiness out is possible. The non-holy animals are unblemished, so making them a תמורה is also possible.

keyTerms.meaning: A dilemma, a question the גמרא is unsure how to answer
Animals that have a blemish (a physical defect)
Non-holy, ordinary animals
Unblemished, whole animals
'These are in place of those'

phrases.english: Abaye asked:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ בַּעֲלוֹת מוּם,
phrases.english: If there were in front of him two holy animals with a blemish,
and two non-holy animals without a blemish,
and he said, "These are in place of those,"
phrases.notes: He says this over the whole group without putting his hand on any one animal, so רב אשי's test from step 5 doesn't help.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב אשי's 'hand position' rule and asks about a case where there is no hand position to decide.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to read 'these in place of those' when it could mean either a תמורה or transferring holiness, and no hand position tells us which.

steps.title: The two sides: making a תמורה with lashes, or choosing the permitted act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the doubt: maybe he meant to make the non-holy animals holy and gets lashes, or maybe we assume a person picks the permitted option over the forbidden one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he mean to put holiness onto the non-holy animals, and so he gets lashes? Or maybe, whenever there is a permitted way to do something, a person does not leave the permitted way and do the forbidden thing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two possible ways to understand the person's words in אביי's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: תחת means making a תמורה. That is forbidden, so he gets lashes. Side two: we assume people act in a permitted way. Transferring holiness out of a blemished holy animal is permitted, so we read his words that way and he gets no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: To make something take on holiness (here, making a תמורה)
He gets lashes
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a doubt)
Something permitted
Something forbidden

keyTerms.term: לָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ הֶיתֵּרָא וְעָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא
keyTerms.meaning: A person does not leave the permitted and do the forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up which act is allowed. Transferring holiness out of a blemished holy animal is the permitted act. Making a תמורה is the forbidden act that brings lashes.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a person does not leave the permitted to do the forbidden is a general way of reading unclear words in the kindest light. אביי's next question depends on it.

phrases.english: Did he mean to put holiness onto them, and so he gets lashes,
or perhaps:
wherever there is a permitted way,
a person does not leave the permitted way
and do the forbidden thing?
phrases.notes: So we would say he meant to move the holiness out of the blemished animals, and he gets no lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר לְאַתְפּוֹסֵי וְלָקֵי אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of אביי's question from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should we read his words as the forbidden act (תמורה, with lashes) or as the permitted act (transferring holiness out)?

steps.title: Follow-up dilemma: one blemished and one unblemished in each group
steps.stepSummary: If we say a person picks the permitted option, אביי asks about two holy animals (one blemished) and two non-holy animals (one blemished) when he says 'these in place of those.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that wherever there is a permitted way, a person does not leave it and do the forbidden thing, then what if there were two holy animals in front of him, one of them blemished, and two non-holy animals, one of them blemished, and he said, 'These are in place of those'? What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the second side of his first question as true and asks a harder follow-up case. The next step explains what makes it unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is an unblemished holy animal. Its holiness cannot be transferred out, so for that animal he must have meant a תמורה. The question is how he meant to match up the animals in each group.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (if we decide the first question this way, then a new question comes up)
One of them

phrases.english: And if you will say,
that wherever there is a permitted way,
a person does not leave it and do the forbidden thing,

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: then if there were in front of him two holy animals,
and one of them was blemished,
and two non-holy animals,
and one of them was blemished,
and he said, "These are in place of those,"
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the second side of step 7 and builds a harder case on top of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: With mixed groups, how did he match up the animals, and which pairing makes a תמורה?

steps.title: First side: he paired them by type
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the doubt: maybe he meant unblemished for unblemished as a תמורה, and blemished for blemished as transferring holiness out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he mean: the unblemished one in place of the unblemished one, to put holiness on it, and the blemished one in place of the blemished one, to take the holiness off it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts laying out the sides of the follow-up question. Here it gives the first possibility, and the other side comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading he matched each animal with one like it. The unblemished pair is a תמורה, which is forbidden and brings lashes. The blemished pair is a permitted transfer of holiness out. So he would get lashes only for the unblemished pair.

keyTerms.meaning: To take holiness off (transfer it from the holy animal onto the non-holy one)
An unblemished animal in place of an unblemished animal

phrases.english: Did he mean:
the unblemished one in place of the unblemished one, to put holiness onto it,

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלַת מוּם תַּחַת בַּעֲלַת מוּם — לְאַחוֹלֵי.
phrases.english: and the blemished one in place of the blemished one, to take the holiness off it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר תְּמִימָה תַּחַת תְּמִימָה לְאַתְפּוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the sides of the follow-up dilemma from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did he match like with like, making only the unblemished pair a תמורה and the blemished pair a transfer of holiness out?

steps.title: The second side of the doubt: crossed pairings, lashes for both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the other possibility: maybe he matched the unblemished non-holy animal with the blemished holy one, and the blemished non-holy animal with the unblemished holy one. If so, both pairings are תמורה and he gets lashes twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe he meant the unblemished non-holy animal to replace the blemished holy one, and the blemished non-holy animal to replace the unblemished holy one. Then he gets lashes for both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining אביי's question from step 8 by giving the second way to read the man's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, only one pairing counted as תמורה. The other was a permitted פדיון of the blemished animal. Here the pairings are crossed, so both count as forbidden תמורה. That means two sets of lashes instead of one.

keyTerms.meaning: An unblemished animal
An animal with a blemish
Holy (consecrated) property
He gets lashes

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
the unblemished non-holy animal
is in place of the blemished holy animal,
and the blemished non-holy animal
is in place of the unblemished holy animal,
and he gets lashes for both?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided doubt begun in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did he pair like with like (one תמורה, one פדיון) or cross them (two תמורות)?

steps.title: Assuming he picks the permitted option, what about three and three?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we answer the last question by saying a person avoids the forbidden when a permitted option exists. Then the blemished holy animal was being redeemed, and he gets no extra lashes. A new case follows: three holy animals (one blemished) and three unblemished non-holy animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you will say that whenever there is a permitted option a person doesn't do the forbidden one, so he meant to redeem and isn't punished, then what if there were three holy animals, one blemished, and three unblemished non-holy animals, and he said, 'These are in place of those'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא assumes an answer to the previous question and uses it to set up a harder case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'a person picks the permitted option' solved the case of two animals on each side. Now all three non-holy animals are unblemished. Two of them must be תמורה for the unblemished holy animals. The question is whether the rule still protects the third pairing, with the blemished holy animal.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say': assume one answer to move on to the next question
The permitted option
The forbidden option
To remove holiness (redeem) onto another animal

phrases.english: And if you will say,
that wherever there is a permitted option
a person does not do the forbidden one,
so he meant to remove the holiness, and he does not get lashes,

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שָׁלֹשׁ בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: if there were before him three holy animals,
and one of them was blemished,
and three non-holy unblemished animals,
and he said: "These are in place of those".

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the 'permitted option' answer to step 8's question and builds a new case on top of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law when every non-holy animal is unblemished and only one holy animal is blemished?

steps.title: The two sides of the three-and-three doubt
steps.stepSummary: One side: since he was clearly making תמורה with the unblemished holy animals, maybe he meant תמורה with the blemished one too. The other side: maybe the 'permitted option' rule still applies, so the last pairing was a redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that since he swapped the unblemished for the unblemished as a תמורה, he also swapped an unblemished for the blemished as a תמורה? Or maybe here too, wherever there is a permitted option he doesn't do the forbidden one, and that last pairing was a redemption?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the three-and-three case is a real doubt by laying out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What is new here is that he has already clearly done forbidden תמורה twice. So maybe his whole statement was meant as תמורה. Or maybe we still read the one pairing that could be permitted in the permitted way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do we say...?': opens the first side of a doubt
To make holiness 'take hold' of a new animal (תמורה)
The last one

phrases.english: Do we say,
since the unblemished in place of the unblemished was meant to put holiness onto them,

phrases.aramaic: תְּמִימוֹת נָמֵי תַּחַת בַּעֲלַת מוּם לְאַתְפּוֹסֵי?
phrases.english: the unblemished in place of the blemished was also meant to put holiness on?
Or perhaps, here too,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶיתֵּירָא לָא עָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא,
phrases.english: wherever there is a permitted option he does not do the forbidden one,
and that last one is to remove holiness.
phrases.notes: 'That last one' is the pairing with the blemished holy animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the doubt raised in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does his clear forbidden intent in the other pairings show what he meant in the blemished pairing?

steps.title: רב אשי asks about four and four
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we answer that someone not yet 'established' as a sinner still picks the permitted option. Then רב אשי asks about four holy animals (one blemished) and four non-holy animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you will say that here too, since the man is not yet established as someone who does forbidden things, he doesn't leave the permitted to do the forbidden, then רב אשי asks: if there were four holy animals, one blemished, and four non-holy animals, and he said 'These are in place of those,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא assumes an answer to the three-and-three case, and רב אשי uses it to ask about a case with four animals on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three and three, he did only two forbidden תמורות. That is not yet a חזקה, which takes three times, so we still assume he picked the permitted option. With four and four, he has done three forbidden תמורות. Maybe now he counts as 'established' in sinning, and we no longer read the blemished pairing in the permitted way.

keyTerms.meaning: Became established (a חזקה, usually after three times)
Leaves aside
Asks a question (a בעיא)
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: The number matters. Three unblemished swaps (in the four-and-four case) may be enough to make him 'established' in doing forbidden things. Two (in the three-and-three case) are not.
steps.whatToRemember: These questions build step by step: 2+2, then 3+3, then 4+4. Each one tests how far the rule 'a person picks the permitted option' goes. A חזקה of three forbidden acts might cancel it.

phrases.english: And if you will say, here too,
since the man still
has not been established as one who does forbidden things,
phrases.notes: In the three-and-three case he did only two forbidden swaps, and it takes three times to be 'established'.

phrases.english: he does not leave the permitted and do the forbidden,
then Rav Ashi asks:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו אַרְבַּע בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: If there were before him four holy animals
and one of them was blemished,
and four non-holy animals,
and he said "These are in place of those," what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר, הָכָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the 'not yet established' answer to step 12 and raises a further case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Once he has done three forbidden תמורות, do we still assume he redeemed the blemished animal?

steps.title: First side: he is clearly a sinner, so four sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: In the four-animal case, maybe the man is now clearly someone who does the forbidden, so all four swaps were תמורה and he gets four sets of lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is certain: since the man has clearly shown he does what is forbidden, he gets four sets of lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first possible answer to רב אשי's question about four holy animals, one of them blemished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the three-animal case we said a man not yet 'established' as a sinner still picks the permitted option. Here he made three clear forbidden swaps first, so maybe he now counts as established. If so, we assume the fourth swap with the blemished animal was also תמורה, which means four sets of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: was established / has a clear track record
the man
sets of lashes
certainly

phrases.english: Here, certainly,
since the man has been established
as doing prohibitions (in all of them),
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. His three clear תמורה swaps show that he does do the forbidden thing.

phrases.english: he is lashed with four sets of lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא וַדַּאי, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיתַּחְזַק גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first side of the four-animal question raised in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the man count as established in sinning once he has made three clear תמורה swaps, so that the fourth swap is also תמורה?

steps.title: Second side: even so, nobody picks the forbidden over the permitted
steps.stepSummary: Maybe even an established sinner would not leave the permitted option to do the forbidden, so the last swap was a redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe, even though he has shown he does the forbidden, a person still does not leave what is permitted to do what is forbidden. If so, the last swap was meant to redeem the blemished animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question: the 'permitted option' rule may apply even to this man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This side says his track record does not change the basic assumption. When he could legally redeem the blemished animal, we assume that is what he meant. Then the fourth pairing is a redemption, and he gets only three sets of lashes.

keyTerms.term: לָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ הֶיתֵּירָא וְעָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא
keyTerms.meaning: a person does not leave the permitted to do the forbidden
to redeem (move the holiness off it)
the last one

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
even though he has been established as doing the prohibition,
a person does not leave the permitted
and do the forbidden,
and so the last one was meant to redeem?
phrases.notes: 'The last one' is the blemished holy animal, which can legally be redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיתַּחְזַק בְּאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the doubt opened in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the 'permitted option' assumption still apply even to someone who has shown he does the forbidden?

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question stands without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole chain of questions, which started with אביי's and ended with רב אשי's, without deciding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each earlier question was only answered for the sake of argument ('ואם תמצי לומר'), so none was really decided. With תיקו, all of them stay a doubt, including the last one: whether the man's track record overrides the 'permitted option' assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: A person is normally assumed to choose the permitted option over the forbidden one. Whether that holds for someone who has already clearly done the forbidden is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the doubt laid out in steps 14 and 15 without deciding it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All of the dilemmas in this chain remain unresolved, ending with the four-animal case.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a blemished holy animal can be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the holy animal was blemished, it becomes non-holy through the exchange.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the holy animal was blemished, it goes out to non-holy status, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the line about a blemished holy animal. This sets up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished holy animal can be redeemed, so the exchange moves its holiness onto the other animal. The משנה also says he must pay the difference in value, and that is what the next argument is about.

keyTerms.meaning: a holy (consecrated) item
blemished animal
goes out to non-holy status (is redeemed)

phrases.english: If the holy animal was blemished,
it goes out to non-holy status, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, that he must pay the difference in value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיָה הֶקְדֵּשׁ בַּעַל מוּם יֹצֵא לְחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה after the תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemished holy animal exchanged for a non-holy one is redeemed.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: redeemed by תורה law, paying the value is only from the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the redemption works by תורה law even for a cheap animal. Paying the full value is a rabbinic rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it goes out to non-holy status by תורה law, and he must pay the value only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the משנה's two parts: the redemption itself and the payment of the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law the holiness moves even if the non-holy animal is worth much less. The רבנן required paying the difference so that הקדש would not lose money.

keyTerms.meaning: by תורה law
to settle the value (pay the difference)
from their words: by rabbinic law

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It goes out to non-holy status by Torah law,
and he must settle the value by their (rabbinic) words,
phrases.notes: He means paying הקדש the difference if the holy animal was worth more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יֹצֵא לְחוּלִּין דְּבַר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה quoted in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Redemption works by תורה law; paying the full value is rabbinic.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: paying the value is also from the תורה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the requirement to pay the full value is itself a תורה law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: paying the value is also required by תורה law.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש disagrees with רבי יוחנן about the payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the requirement to pay the value comes from the תורה, not only from the רבנן. Both agree there is a payment. They argue only about how strong the requirement is.

keyTerms.meaning: also / even

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש require paying the difference. The argument is only whether that rule comes from the תורה or from the רבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the redemption works by תורה law and paying the value is rabbinic. ריש לקיש: paying the value is also a תורה law.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּמִים דְּבַר תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: Settling the value is also required by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אַף צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּמִים דְּבַר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן's view in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The requirement to pay the full value is a תורה law.

steps.title: What case is the argument about? Maybe a one-sixth gap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are arguing about. It tests the idea that it is a case of אונאה, a gap of exactly one-sixth, and asks whether ריש לקיש would call the payment a תורה law there.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If we say it is a case of overcharging (a gap of exactly one-sixth), would ריש לקיש say that even here one must pay the full value by תורה law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to pin down which case the argument from steps 18-19 is about. It tries the first option, a gap of exactly one-sixth, and already sounds doubtful about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a regular sale, a gap of exactly one-sixth is אונאה: the sale stands, but the extra money must be returned. If the argument were about that case, ריש לקיש would be saying that the תורה's אונאה rules apply to holy property. The question 'would ריש לקיש really say that?' sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
Overcharging by exactly one-sixth. The sale stands, but the difference is returned.
To make up the value, meaning to pay the full worth
By תורה law

phrases.english: What are we dealing with?
If we say it is about overcharging,
phrases.notes: Overcharging here means a gap of exactly one-sixth between the two animals' values.

phrases.english: in this case would ריש לקיש say
that one even needs to make up the value
by Torah law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִי נֵימָא אַאוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what exact case the argument in steps 18-19 is about, and tests the first option.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which price gap the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש is about.

steps.title: Holy property has no overcharging law
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that consecrated property is not covered by the אונאה rules. So ריש לקיש could not be saying that a one-sixth gap must be paid back by תורה law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: These are things that have no overcharging law: slaves, documents, lands, and consecrated property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that knocks out the first option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists הקדשות, holy property, among the things the אונאה rules do not cover. If the תורה's overcharging rule does not apply to holy property at all, ריש לקיש could not base a תורה-level payment on it. So the argument cannot be about a gap of exactly one-sixth.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated property, things given to the בית המקדש
Land
Documents, such as loan papers

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
These are things that have no overcharging law:
slaves, and documents,
and lands, and consecrated property!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a משנה to reject the one-sixth option from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that ריש לקיש is talking about an אונאה case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holy property is not covered by the אונאה rules, so no תורה-level payment can come from them.
steps.whatToRemember: Holy property (הקדשות) is not covered by the אונאה rules, so the argument cannot be about a one-sixth gap.

steps.title: Maybe a gap of more than one-sixth? Then רבי יוחנן is hard to explain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a second option: the argument is about בטול מקח, a gap bigger than one-sixth. But it asks whether רבי יוחנן could really say that paying the full value is only rabbinic in such a case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about cancellation of a sale (a gap bigger than one-sixth). In this case would רבי יוחנן say that one needs to make up the value only rabbinically?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to a second option for the case, but it immediately challenges רבי יוחנן's side. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a regular sale, a gap bigger than one-sixth cancels the sale completely. If the argument is about that kind of gap, it sounds strange for רבי יוחנן to say the exchange works by תורה law and paying the full value is only a rabbinic rule. So the second option seems to cause trouble for רבי יוחנן instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier suggestion and offers a new one.
Cancellation of a sale, which happens when the price gap is more than one-sixth
By rabbinic law

phrases.english: Rather, it is about cancellation of a sale,
phrases.notes: This means a gap bigger than one-sixth, which cancels a regular sale.

phrases.english: so in this case would רבי יוחנן say
that one needs to make up the value only by rabbinic law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אַבִּטּוּל מִקָּח בְּהָא נֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the one-sixth option is rejected, the גמרא offers the bigger-gap option and challenges רבי יוחנן with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that paying the full value is only rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gap bigger than one-sixth cancels a regular sale, so calling the payment only rabbinic in that case sounds too weak.
steps.confusionAlert: Remember the two price gaps: exactly one-sixth is אונאה (the sale stands, the extra is returned), and more than one-sixth is בטול מקח (the sale is cancelled).
